2025_139_m121724bdmtg.paragraph: Minutes of the Troy Board of Education regular meeting held December 17, 2024 at the Services Building, 4420 Livernois, called to order at 7:00 p.m. by Vice President Anne with Board members Alic, Hauff, Haupt and Philippart present and President Schmidt and Dr. Wilson absent. The Board's two substantive actions were awards from the 2023 Capital Projects Fund for the district's playground program: $2,566,375.57 for Phase 2 playground equipment and installation split between Sinclair Rec/GameTime and Midstate Rec/Playworld, and $3,767,447.16 for playground site work, landscaping and asphalt paving including contingency. The meeting adjourned at 8:36 p.m. following tributes to retiring member Gary N. Hauff.

**Meeting Identification**
Troy Board of Education regular meeting, December 17, 2024, Troy School District Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, Michigan. Minutes signed by Gary N. Hauff, Secretary, Troy Board of Education (clerical notation GH/jh).

**Attendance**
Vice President Anne called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m. Present in addition to Mrs. Anne: Board members Alic, Hauff, Haupt and Philippart. Absent: President Schmidt and Dr. Wilson. Also present: Superintendent Machesky and administrators Montante, DiPilato, Griffor, Pagel, Burden and Trudell. Approximately 75 members of the audience attended.

**Recognition and Mission Moment**
Athens High School was recognized for hosting American Red Cross blood drives, with Carmen Timm of the American Red Cross honoring teachers Shawn DuFresne and Deanna Fakhouri and students Claire Kilbride, Maggie Ianev, Everett Marshall, Willow Bodendorfer and Jack Appledorn, who run blood drives to earn scholarship money. Troy High students who attended the Global Leadership Summit in Berlin, Germany the previous summer were also recognized; they travelled to the French Riviera, Switzerland and Berlin studying the Impact of Water on Society among 1,100 students from around the world. Adviser and Communications Instructor Harriet Clark introduced the participants. The Student Spotlight featured Ryan Stasinski, an Athens High School senior in the TSD Creative Guild, presented by Thomas Butcher.

**Student Representative Reports**
Nurayda Albeez (International Academy-East), Kristian Vitanovich (Troy College and Career High School), Madie Miller (Troy High School, filling in for Adam McManus), and Diana D'Aloisio (Athens High School) reported on school events and activities.

**Consent Agenda**
Moved by Mr. Hauff, supported by Mr. Haupt, to approve items A, B, C and D: minutes of the November 12, 2024 Board Workshop; minutes of the November 19, 2024 Board Meeting; Treasurer's Report for October 2024; and Budget Amendment #1. Yes: 5. No: 0. Absent: Schmidt, Wilson. There were no additions or deletions, no public communication on agenda items, and no personnel or curriculum items.

**Business - Playground Equipment Purchase Phase 2**
Moved by Mr. Haupt, supported by Mrs. Alic, awarding the bid for playground equipment and installation as an expenditure of the 2023 Capital Projects Fund. Yes: 5. No: 0. Absent: Schmidt, Wilson.

| Award | Vendor | Amount |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Playground Equipment, Contractor #1 | Sinclair Rec/GameTime | $1,246,295.60 |
| Playground Equipment, Contractor #2 | Midstate Rec/Playworld | $1,320,079.97 |
| Total | | $2,566,375.57 |

**Business - Playground Site Work**
Moved by Dr. Philippart, supported by Mrs. Alic, awarding the site work bid as an expenditure of the 2023 Capital Projects Fund. Yes: 5. No: 0. Absent: Schmidt, Wilson.

| Scope | Contractor | Schools | Amount |

| Sitework2 | Cortis Brothers T&E | Leonard, Schroeder, Wass | $961,100.00 |
| Landscape1 | Santoro Services | Costello, Hamilton, Wattles | $426,490.00 |
| Landscape2 | Dalco Landscape | Leonard, Schroeder, Wass | $495,250.00 |
| Asphalt Paving | Asphalt Specialties | | $731,000.00 |
| Contingency | | | $279,070.16 |
| Total | | | $3,767,447.16 |

**Public Communication and Closing**
Seven community members addressed the Board during non-agenda public communication; no action was taken. Board members thanked Mr. Hauff for his dedication and years of service, and he noted his nearly 26 years on the Troy School Board. The Board congratulated and welcomed Audra Melton, Ayesha Potts and Stephanie Zendler. Mrs. Anne announced the next Board Workshop at Baker Middle School on January 14th at 6:00 p.m. and the Organizational and Regular Board Meeting on January 21st at the Services Building at 7:00 p.m. The meeting adjourned at 8:36 p.m.
2025_139_m121724bdmtg.verbose:
Official minutes of the Troy Board of Education regular board meeting held December 17, 2024 at the Troy School District Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, Michigan. The record carries the clerical notation GH/jh and is submitted by Gary N. Hauff, Secretary, Troy Board of Education.

CALL TO ORDER AND ATTENDANCE
Vice President Anne called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m. In addition to Mrs. Anne, Board members Alic, Hauff, Haupt and Philippart were present. President Schmidt and Dr. Wilson were absent. Also present were Superintendent Machesky and administrators Montante, DiPilato, Griffor, Pagel, Burden and Trudell. Approximately 75 members of the audience attended.

RECOGNITION - AMERICAN RED CROSS, ATHENS HIGH SCHOOL BLOOD DRIVES
The Board recognized Athens High School, which was selected to be honored by the American Red Cross for its support in hosting blood drives in the community. Carmen Timm of the American Red Cross attended to recognize Athens teachers Shawn DuFresne and Deanna Fakhouri along with their students, who run blood drives during the school year to earn scholarship money. Students called forward for recognition were Claire Kilbride, Maggie Ianev, Everett Marshall, Willow Bodendorfer and Jack Appledorn.

MISSION MOMENT - TROY HIGH STUDENTS, LEADERSHIP SUMMIT IN GERMANY
The Board recognized Troy High Colts who attended the Global Leadership Summit in Berlin, Germany during the prior summer. Selected on leadership and outstanding character, the students travelled to the French Riviera, Switzerland and Berlin exploring the Impact of Water on Society, seeking to better understand water's influence on transportation, agriculture, energy and more. They were among 1,100 students from around the world studying water's impact in other European countries. During the summit, students were placed in teams and charged with solving a global problem related to the theme of water; using design thinking they ideated and created a prototype and delivered a one-minute pitch on the prototype to the judges. Communications Instructor and Global Leadership Summit Adviser Harriet Clark was invited to describe the competition and introduce her students, recognizing Ashley Carron, Anusha Gupta, Ava Fleming, Jake Baker, Josie Lido, Katerina Zak, Kate Bestul, Vivian Edoff, Nicole Gherase, Laith Hermiz, Nainika Jasti, Keira McComb, Shreyan Maini, Maya Saad, Neel Nagappala and Tia Tonelli.

STUDENT SPOTLIGHT
The Student Spotlight segment recognizes the talents and achievements of students in the TSD Creative Guild. The spotlight fell on Ryan Stasinski, a senior from Athens High School with a unique passion for sports; Thomas Butcher attended to describe the student's work.

REPORTS FROM HIGH SCHOOL STUDENT REPRESENTATIVES
Nurayda Albeez, student representative for International Academy-East, shared a report on events and activities at her school. Kristian Vitanovich, student representative for Troy College and Career High School, reported on events and activities at TCCHS. Madie Miller, student representative for Troy High School, filled in for Adam McManus, who was not present, and shared a report on events and activities at her school. Diana D'Aloisio, student representative for Athens High School, reported on events and activities at Athens.

ADDITIONS AND DELETIONS; PUBLIC COMMUNICATION ON AGENDA ITEMS
There were no additions or deletions to the agenda, and no public communication on agenda items.

GENERAL - CONSENT AGENDA
It was moved by Mr. Hauff and supported by Mr. Haupt that the Troy Board of Education take action to approve items A, B, C and D on the consent agenda. The items were: minutes of the November 12, 2024 Board of Education Workshop; minutes of the November 19, 2024 Board of Education Meeting; the Treasurer's Report for October 2024; and Budget Amendment #1. The vote was Yes: 5, No: 0, with Schmidt and Wilson recorded absent.

PERSONNEL AND CURRICULUM
No personnel items and no curriculum items were presented.

BUSINESS - PLAYGROUND EQUIPMENT PURCHASE PHASE 2
It was moved by Mr. Haupt and supported by Mrs. Alic that the bid for playground equipment and installation be awarded as set out below and that the amount be approved as an expenditure of the 2023 Capital Projects Fund. The awards were: Sinclair Rec/GameTime, Playground Equipment, Contractor #1, $1,246,295.60; and Midstate Rec/Playworld, Playground Equipment, Contractor #2, $1,320,079.97. The stated total was $2,566,375.57. The vote was Yes: 5, No: 0, Absent: Schmidt, Wilson.

BUSINESS - PLAYGROUND SITE WORK
It was moved by Dr. Philippart and supported by Mrs. Alic that the bid for playground site work be awarded as set out below and that the amount be approved as an expenditure of the 2023 Capital Projects Fund. The award schedule listed: Sitework1 to Santoro Services, $874,537.00, covering Costello, Hamilton and Wattles; Sitework2 to Cortis Brothers T&E, $961,100.00, covering Leonard, Schroeder and Wass; Landscape1 to Santoro Services, $426,490.00, covering Costello, Hamilton and Wattles; Landscape2 to Dalco Landscape, $495,250.00, covering Leonard, Schroeder and Wass; and Asphalt Paving to Asphalt Specialties, $731,000.00. The minutes state a Bid Total of $3,488,377.00 (rendered in the document text as "$3,488.377.00"), a Contingency of $279,070.16, and a TOTAL of $3,767,447.16. The vote was Yes: 5, No: 0, Absent: Schmidt, Wilson. Together with the equipment award, the six elementary sites named across the two site work packages are Costello, Hamilton, Wattles, Leonard, Schroeder and Wass.

PUBLIC COMMUNICATION - NON-AGENDA ITEMS
Seven community members addressed the Board during public communication. No action was taken by the Board.

OTHER
No items were presented under Other.

BOARD COMMENTS
Board members shared sentiments about Mr. Hauff and thanked him for his dedication and years of service as a board member to the Troy School District students and community. Board members also congratulated Audra Melton, Ayesha Potts and Stephanie Zendler and welcomed them to the Troy Board of Education. Mr. Hauff shared his sentiments on how happy he was to have served on the Troy School Board for almost 26 years and acknowledged his appreciation for many members of the Troy School District team. Mrs. Anne announced that the next Board Workshop would be held at Baker Middle School on January 14th at 6:00 p.m., and that the Organizational and Regular Board Meeting would be held on January 21st in the Services Building at 7:00 p.m.

ADJOURNMENT
The meeting adjourned at 8:36 p.m. The minutes were respectfully submitted by Gary N. Hauff, Secretary, Troy Board of Education.
